title: introduce-varint-prefixed-sse-frames-and-late-arrival-replay-handshake
author: Eleanor Chen
description: Motivation: intermittent partial JSON and delimiter misalignment in high-concurrency SSE streams were causing structured-toolcall boundaries to be lost when fragments arrived out of order or when proxies coalesced chunks. This PR introduces a small, backward-compatible binary preface (varint length) for compound SSE events plus a lightweight late-arrival replay/repair handshake to avoid relying solely on textual delimiters. Design summary: 1) Each application-level SSE payload (the JSON blob that represents a chunk of assistant output or a toolcall sentinel) is optionally prefixed with a compact varint length header when negotiated by the client via an upgraded header (X-Redwood-SSE-Frame: varint-v1). 2) The server-side reassembly layer uses the varint preface to atomically extract full JSON spans even when newline/"data:" delimiters are split or coalesced by middleware. 3) For clients that cannot use the prefixed frames, we preserve the existing textual delimiter parser; the change is feature-gated and enabled by default only on new connections. 4) A late-arrival repair handshake allows a short ack/replay window: when the reassembly layer detects a gap (sequence id delta) it emits a compact RESYNC notice into the stream and will replay the last N events for that connection from an in-memory soft-cache so downstream consumers can reconcile partial JSON without triggering toolcall misfires. Compatibility: maintains OpenAI-compatibility mode for existing clients, negotiates via initial SSE headers and falls back on textual parsing when negotiation fails. Performance: microbenchmarks on p3.2xlarge show a median 2.1% CPU overhead at 10k concurrent short streams, and a 38% reduction in observed partial-json parse failures in fuzz tests. Rollout plan: gated rollout behind a feature flag and connection header; staged traffic on canary region for 48h then global. Backports: candidate for 1.18.x runtime patch if validated in canary. QA and testing: unit tests for varint framing, integration tests for mixed clients (prefixed+text), fuzz corpus extended with proxy coalescing patterns. Checklist: - [x] varint framing encode/decode - [x] negotiation header and fallback path - [x] soft-cache replay implementation and memory guardrails - [x] integration tests with function/toolcall boundaries - [x] smoke in canary and load tests - [x] updated docs and SDK notes (Python/TS) Related work: follows up on ENG-1994 and addresses incidents SUP-9910 and notes from the streaming stability runbook. Merge: squash and merge.

files_summary: varint.go: compact LE varint encode/decode with boundary checks and UTF-8 preservation
stream_reassembler.go: prefer varint-prefixed frames when negotiated; fall back to legacy parser
replay_cache.go: ring-buffer soft-cache with per-connection memory cap and TTL
sse_shim.go: proxy shim to preserve preface across intermediate proxying
sdk changes: small opt-in examples and negotiation helper functions
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can we make the replay window configurable per connection and bound to X MB? I'm worried about memory spikes under many short-lived connections.

Eleanor Chen (author): Answer: yes, replay window is configurable via feature flag and deploy/featureflags/flags.yaml defaults to 1MB per connection; soft-cache enforces eviction and per-node global cap to avoid OOM.
Maya Patel: Tests look good; please add a flamegraph from the load test for reference in the PR so ops can verify the reported 2.1% CPU uplift.
Eleanor Chen (author): Added load test artifacts and a brief perf note to docs/streaming/varint_preface.md.
Ravi Singh: One nit: use unsigned varints to avoid sign-extension weirdness and add a max-frame-size guard to avoid O(n^2) parsing when a client sends a huge length.
Eleanor Chen (author): Updated parser to use uvarint and added hard cap of 1MB for prefixed frames; fallback behavior documented.
merge_details: squash merged by Maya Patel into main; commit message: 'sse: optional varint-prefixed frames + late-arrival replay handshake to reduce partial-json failures and stabilize toolcall boundaries', CI green at merge
release_notes: Stabilize streaming structured output: optional varint-prefixed SSE frames to prevent partial-JSON and delimiter-splitting bugs; late-arrival replay/resync handshake reduces toolcall misfires. Opt-in via X-Redwood-SSE-Frame header; negotiated by default on new connections. Backwards compatible with legacy clients.
